links.note: Toy and public parameters only; planted discrete logs on constructed toy curves. A design: nothing here has been run beyond the sub-minute feasibility probes in probe/.

question: For the explicit Legendre fibre family L_t0: y^2 = x(x+1)(x+t0) specialised from F_p(u), u^(p+1) = t0, does the family of known sections (traces of P(u) = (u, u(u+1)^((p+1)/2)), u in the norm-t0 coset of mu_(p+1) in F_(p^2)) (1) cover fibres and targets Q like a random subset of the same size, (2) show any mu_(p+1)-character structure in the discrete logs of those sections, and (3) allow a lift to be found below the cost of the best generic meet-in-the-middle, and if so does the complete discrete-log cost built on it stay above matched rho?

claims.text: Every reported representation Q = sum of signed section traces verifies by an independent group computation, and every planted instance is recovered.

Coverage of G by weight-w sums of family traces (w = 1, 2) equals the random-subset control within the A/A spread, stratified by square class; any shortfall in E(F_p) is accounted for by the stratum restriction.
claims.if_supported: no coverage structure beyond the square-class restriction at these sizes
claims.if_not_supported: coverage structure in G: a lead, to be explained algebraically before any use

claims.text: The maximum normalised mu_(p+1) x Z/N Fourier coefficient of the section logs does not exceed the orbit-respecting permutation null, for fibre and for target-residual statistics, at a power the positive control certifies.
claims.if_supported: within the null: no character bias at the certified detectable fraction
claims.if_not_supported: a bias, with its dependence on fibre or target tabulated

claims.text: The per-lift counted cost of the table-free torus finder scales below the best generic meet-in-the-middle finder on the same instances (exponent intervals disjoint over the ladder).
claims.if_supported: the knapsack reading of the lift step is wrong for w = 2: membership in the norm torus is algebraic and table-free
claims.if_not_supported: the finder is not below meet-in-the-middle

claims.text: The complete discrete-log cost built from the finder (relations plus linear algebra, all charged) has fitted exponent above 1/2 and a ratio to matched rho that does not decrease over the ladder.
claims.if_supported: closure stands, with the obstruction restated as relation count and linear algebra, not a knapsack
claims.if_not_supported: reopen the lift route (exponent interval below 1/2, or ratio to rho falling over the ladder to below 1)

hypotheses.statement: The specialisation is a generic homomorphism: the family's traces behave as a random subset of G of the same size (coverage, characters), a lift exists by counting but the complete cost is at least that of generic meet-in-the-middle and above rho.
hypotheses.mechanism: No morphism from the genus-0 torus to E_t0; the function-field lattice contributes about 2 free relations among p+1 specialised points.

predictions.minimum_effect: family and random-subset coverage differ by less than the A/A half-width at every size

arms.description: Generic meet-in-the-middle finder: sees only group elements of the family items, table of K items, probes Q minus random item; K on the grid sqrt(N)*{1/4,1/2,1,2,4}, best median per size is the reference.
Pollard rho with negation map on G, counted in the same unit, the denominator of the complete-cost ratio.

Table-free torus finder: random u1, residual R = Q - Tr P(u1), solve the degree <= 4 polynomial in the torus parameter from S_3(x(tau), x(tau)^p, x(R)) = 0, accept preimages; complete-solve variant restricts u to a subgroup coset of index s and runs sparse elimination mod N.

parameters.subgroup_index_rule: s = round(sqrt(p+1)) rounded to a divisor of p+1

arms.description: The candidate repeated under a disjoint seed stream and with fibres split into two halves by a seeded hash bit; differs only in nuisance seed and split.

Positive control through the same code path: Q is built as a known signed sum of one or two family traces (finder must return a valid representation), and the character test runs on logs with a planted periodic component replacing a fraction eps in {0.05, 0.10, 0.25} of positions.

Negative control: a uniformly random subset of E(F_p) of the same distinct size as the family's trace set, assigned to the same involution orbits at random; coverage, character test and meet-in-the-middle run unchanged. The table-free finder is not defined on it (no algebraic membership).

positive.expected_detection: finder returns a valid representation on 100% of planted instances; the character test detects eps = 0.25 at every size and its smallest detected eps per size is reported as the sensitivity

null_population.description: uniform random subsets of E(F_p), without replacement, of the family's distinct trace-set size, assigned to the same involution orbits at random
null_population.generator: SHA-256-seeded Fisher-Yates over E(F_p) of the same fibres; one subset per fibre per replicate
null_population.why_n: 6 sizes x 16 fibres; enough for a Kolmogorov-Smirnov uniformity check of the character-test p-values at 0.01

independent.name: item_set
levels: random subset of the same size

factors.name: prime_p
factors.how: ladder: coverage and character arms k in {8,9,10,11,12,13}, finder arms k in {10,12,14,16,18,20,22}; p is the largest prime below 2^k

factors.name: fibre_t0
factors.how: first T accepted in the order of SHA-256('ulmer-ctl-v1'|p|i) mod (p-2) + 2; accepted iff the largest prime factor N of |E| is at least |E|/16; T = 16 (arms 1-2), 8 (arm 3); independent of arm

factors.name: target_Q
factors.how: arm 1: all of G; arm 3: 64 per fibre from SHA-256('ulmer-ctl-v1-Q'|p|t0|j) as a scalar of the prime-order generator; independent of arm

factors.name: field_representation
factors.value: F_(p^2) = F_p[s]/(s^2 - n), n the least non-residue; Legendre form

factors.name: unit_charges
factors.value: add 1I+2M+1S, double 1I+2M+2S (+1M for the a2 constant), F_(p^2) mul 4M, sqr 2M+1S+1M, F_(p^2) inversion 1I+2M+2S+2M; hash probe and insert counted apart and also priced at 1M in a sensitivity row
factors.how: one instrumented field type counting every call

factors.name: binary
factors.how: one binary, sha256 recorded; counts do not depend on it

factors.name: threads
factors.how: single thread per row; rows parallel across processes only

factors.name: host_load
factors.how: no clock is a metric; load recorded per row for completeness

factors.name: seed_stream
factors.how: algorithm seeds from the protocol hash; A/A uses stream B

factors.name: arm_order
factors.how: arms interleaved per instance; counts are order independent

seed_derivation.note: every seed is SHA-256(protocol_sha256 | arm_stream | p | t0 | index); the fibre and target rules above use a fixed label so fibres and targets are shared by all arms, not arm-dependent

instance_sampling.rule: fibres and targets by the SHA-256 rules in the variable ledger, frozen before data; the primes by the largest-prime-below-2^k rule

blinding.how: experiment_protocol.py blind masks arm names and control roles; the frozen analysis script runs on the masked copy first
blinding.unmasked_at: after the analysis outputs are written

power.note: character test: 19,999 orbit-respecting null resamples per size, add-one doubled smaller tail, min 2/20000 = 1.0e-4 below alpha/m = 0.001/6 = 1.67e-4; six sizes. Cost arm: 7 sizes x 8 fibres x 64 targets = 3584 targets, exponents fitted per fibre with a two-stage bootstrap over fibres then targets. Power to detect a character bias is certified by the positive control at eps in {0.05, 0.10, 0.25}, not by this arithmetic.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: estimate from the probe (python, p <= 31 in 0.3 s) scaled to Rust; to be replaced by one timed call per arm before freezing

primary.name: coverage of G
primary.definition: |{Q in G : Q is a signed sum of at most w distinct projected trace points}| / |G| after multiplying by the cofactor, w = 1, 2, exhaustive

primary.name: max character coefficient
primary.definition: max over k in 1..(p+1)/2 and a in 1..16 of |sum_j e(kj/(p+1)) e(a ell_j / N)| / sqrt(orbits), ell_j = log_G(h Tr P(g^j u0)), compared with the max of the same statistic on 19,999 orbit-respecting permutations; also the target-residual version with ell replaced by log(Q - Tr)
primary.formula: z = max_{k,a}|sum_j exp(2 pi i (k j/(p+1) + a ell_j/N))| / sqrt(orbits); p_value = (1 + #{null z' >= z}) / (1 + 19999)

primary.name: per-lift cost
primary.unit: field multiplication equivalents (M + S + I*ratio) per verified weight-2 representation
primary.definition: all instrumented F_p calls from receiving Q to a verified representation, item generation included, table setup shown separately and added in the single-target total

primary.name: complete discrete-log cost
primary.definition: relation phase (finder calls) plus sparse elimination mod N (one multiplication mod N charged as one M, listed apart) plus the final recovery and verification; the same unit for rho.negation on G

secondary.name: coverage by square-class stratum of E(F_p)
secondary.definition: coverage_g computed on each coset of 2E(F_p)

secondary.name: torus preimages of a trace
secondary.definition: number of u in the norm-t0 coset with Tr P(u) = R, excluding R in E[2]

secondary.name: isomorphism classes of full-2-torsion curves hit by fibres
secondary.definition: classes among all (c4, c6) up to u^4, u^6 scaling with full rational 2-torsion that equal some fibre, p < 1100

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: all fibres, targets and null resamples listed above, then stop; no sequential extension
a row whose representation fails the independent group check is recorded as wrong_answer and stops nothing

invalidation_rules: a row whose verification fails is excluded from cost medians and counted in the flow
a fibre with N < |E|/16 is not accepted (selection rule, applied before any data)
wall time is never a metric

decision_rule.text: Disposition after the run. (a) Closure stands, obstruction restated: C2 and C3 supported, C5 supported (complete-solve exponent interval above 1/2 and ratio to rho non-decreasing); this holds whether or not C4 is supported. (b) C4 supported alone is recorded as a correction to the report's wording, not a reopening. (c) Reopen LEAD-ICP-xedni-function-field-sections and LEAD-TRF-function-field-xedni-lift: C5 not supported, or C3 not supported with a dependence on t0 or Q that reproduces across the A/A split, or C2 not supported in G. (d) Invalid: positive control misses eps = 0.25, A/A exceeds the null, or the negative control p-values fail a Kolmogorov-Smirnov uniformity test at 0.01.
decision_rule.threshold: exponent intervals disjoint for C4; complete-solve exponent lower bound above 0.5 for C5; null p below 0.001/6 for C3; coverage gap above the A/A half-width at four of six sizes for C2
decision_rule.statistic: fitted exponent of median cost against N per arm; Fourier-maximum rank against the orbit null; coverage difference against the random-subset control
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: exponent difference; ratio of totals to rho; coverage difference

outputs: character table with null percentiles and positive-control sensitivity

graphs: coverage by stratum against the random-subset control
max character z against the null with the planted sensitivity
per-lift and complete cost against N with fitted exponents

inadmissible: changing the ladder, fibre rule, weights, subgroup index rule, grid of K or unit charges after seeing any result
reading a per-lift cost below meet-in-the-middle as a discrete-log speedup without the complete-solve ratio to rho
letting any finder read a discrete log table of the items (the generic finders see group elements only)
reporting coverage of E(F_p) without the square-class stratification, or a character test without the orbit-respecting null
tuning the meet-in-the-middle grid per instance, or restricting the reference to a table size worse than the grid minimum
any wall-clock number as a result; any statement about a deployed key or a curve of cryptographic size
